figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of the observability-aligned framework. Offline training (top): a spatiotemporal diffusion prior is trained on clean simulated sources. The singular value decomposition (SVD) of the lead field splits each source into row and null components, from which a ridge map and a residual TCN acting in a null-space basis are fitted. Test-time inference (bottom): Stage I refines the MNE-initialized row component with singular-coordinate Posterior-DDIM. Stage II adds the frozen ridge and TCN null-space completions, which leave the predicted EEG unchanged.

Fig. 2. Lead-field sensitivity and directional reconstruction error. (a) Relative singular spectrum. (b) Mean paired RRE reduction (MNE minus the updated Posterior-DDIM implementation) on 60 validation identities, four SNRs, and four noise repeats (960 observations), before null-space completion. Repeats are averaged within identity. Teal indicates lower error; the color scale is symmetric logarithmic. Strong, middle, and weak groups comprise directions 1–13, 14–51, and 52–64.

Fig. 3. Multiview comparison for a four-source simulation at 10 dB. The top row shows the ground truth, Ours, MNE, and ConvDip, and the bottom row shows eLORETA, sLORETA, XDL-ESI, and dSPM. Each map shows the temporal RMS over 128 frames in left-lateral, right-lateral, superior, and posterior views. Interpolated maps are peak-normalized separately within each hemisphere, share one color scale across views, and are colored only above 35%. AUC and symmetric geodesic LE are computed from the original node waveforms at prediction threshold 0.1, not at the display threshold. This single illustration is not a randomly sampled performance estimate.

TABLE II ROW-INPUT AND COMPLETION ABLATIONS ON THE TEST SET AT PREDICTION THRESHOLD 0.1. DEPLOYMENT ROWS USE 8,000 EEG OBSERVATIONS; THE EXACT-ROW DIAGNOSTIC SUPPLIES THE GROUND-TRUTH ROW COMPONENT OF THE 2,000 TEST IDENTITIES. BOLD MARKS THE BEST DEPLOYMENT VALUE. VALUES ARE MEAN ± SD ACROSS 2,000 IDENTITIES; FOUR SNRS ARE AVERAGED WITHIN IDENTITY FOR DEPLOYMENT ROWS.

TABLE IV LOCALIZATION BENCHMARK BY SNR. VALUES ARE MEAN ± SD ACROSS 2,000 TEST IDENTITIES PER SNR (8,000 OBSERVATIONS PER METHOD). SD DESCRIBES BETWEEN-IDENTITY VARIATION FOR FIXED MODELS, NOT TRAINING-SEED VARIABILITY. HIGHER AUC, AP, AND F1 AND LOWER SYMMETRIC LE (MM) ARE BETTER. BOLD MARKS THE BEST MEAN IN EACH COLUMN.

Fig. 4. MNE sample peak localization for (a) left ear, (b) right ear, (c) left visual field, and (d) right visual field. Each condition shows MEG-dSPM and Ours at the source-maximum time of Ours, in left-lateral, right-lateral, and posterior views. Cyan stars mark the global MEG peak, cyan diamonds the other-hemisphere auditory MEG peak, and green circles the peak of Ours. Distances d are measured in canonical three-dimensional source coordinates, not in the displayed projections. Absolute maps are independently whole-brain peak-normalized, with shared linear magma color and square-root opacity and no threshold. MEG is a cross-modal reference, not ground truth.

Fig. 5. Coreg-spikes sub-01 reconstruction from the average of 71 spike-aligned EEG epochs. Ours denotes the individual-geometry Posterior-DDIM row + ridge + TCN pipeline. Six views show the same peak-normalized absolute source map at 26 ms, the time of the space–time source maximum over −10 to 100 ms. Cyan stars mark the projected SEEG contact, and green circles mark the reconstruction peak; the two are 22.98 mm apart in three dimensions. All views share one normalization, and no threshold is applied. Projected markers need not lie on the visible surface.
